pastMedicalHistory: Recent left total knee arthroplasty 10 days ago

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden severe syncope, dyspnea, and crushing substernal chest pressure
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Sudden collapse while walking to bathroom 20 minutes ago

releasedFindings: Physical exam: Profound jugular venous distention to the angle of the jaw; clear lungs bilaterally on auscultation.

Bedside echocardiogram (FOCUS): Severe right ventricular dilation (RV/LV diameter ratio > 1.2), McConnell sign (RV free wall hypokinesis with preserved apical contractility), and paradoxical interventricular septal flattening ('D-shaped' left ventricle).
12-Lead ECG: Sinus tachycardia at 138 bpm with classic S1Q3T3 pattern and T-wave inversions across V1-V4.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Massive high-risk pulmonary embolism presenting with acute obstructive shock and RV failure; immediate indication for systemic thrombolysis or catheter-directed embolectomy; avoid aggressive fluid boluses which worsen RV wall tension and ischemia.

releasedFindings: Patient is too hemodynamically unstable to transfer to CT scanner for CTPA.
Bedside lower extremity ultrasound demonstrates non-compressible left common femoral vein thrombus.
Serum Troponin I is 0.48 ng/mL; Serum Lactate is 5.4 mmol/L.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirmed massive PE with hemodynamic collapse; CTPA is deferred due to instability; proceed immediately to systemic thrombolytic therapy (Alteplase 100 mg IV over 2 hours or accelerated 50 mg push in cardiac arrest) with simultaneous Norepinephrine infusion.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Massive High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism with Acute Obstructive Shock
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Sustained hypotension (SBP < 90 mmHg), acute RV dilation with McConnell sign on bedside echo, elevated troponin/lactate, and S1Q3T3 ECG pattern in a high-risk post-orthopedic surgery patient.

rankedDifferential.condition: Massive Pulmonary Embolism with Obstructive Shock

clinicalScores.formula: Age + Male + Cancer + Heart Failure + Chronic Lung + Pulse >= 110 + SBP < 100 + RR >= 30 + Temp < 36 + Altered Mental + SpO2 < 90
clinicalScores.expectedResult: PESI Class V (Very High 30-Day Mortality Risk > 20%)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Assign points strictly for verified vital/clinical derangements.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Assess RV strain, McConnell sign, and rule out tamponade.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Serum Lactate and High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Quantify tissue hypoperfusion and right ventricular myocardial injury.

immediateInterventions: Immediate systemic thrombolytic therapy: IV Alteplase (tPA) 100 mg infusion over 2 hours
Titrate Norepinephrine or Epinephrine infusion to support RV perfusion pressure (target MAP >= 65 mmHg)
Avoid large crystalloid fluid boluses (limit to <= 500 mL) to prevent RV overdistention
Unfractionated Heparin infusion without bolus if thrombolysis given
definitiveTherapy: Emergency surgical embolectomy or catheter-directed thrombectomy if thrombolysis fails or is contraindicated

strictContraindications: Aggressive fluid resuscitation (> 1,000 mL crystalloid) which causes fatal RV chamber dilation and septal shift
Transporting an unstable hypotensive patient away from the resuscitation bay for CTPA
highRiskInteractions: Fluid overload in acute cor pulmonale increases RV wall tension, compresses the RCA, and precipitates circulatory arrest.

criticalFailures.description: Giving aggressive fluid boluses instead of inotropic/vasopressor support and thrombolysis in massive PE shock

guidelineReferences.organization: European Society of Cardiology / European Respiratory Society
guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Persistent vomiting, profound weakness, and deep rapid breathing
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Symptoms developed over past 36 hours during acute viral gastroenteritis

releasedFindings: Fingerstick blood glucose is unexpectedly only 172 mg/dL (below standard DKA threshold of 250 mg/dL).
Venous Blood Gas: pH 7.14, pCO2 22 mmHg, HCO3 7 mmol/L (severe metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation).
Basic Metabolic Panel: Sodium 132 mEq/L, Potassium 4.8 mEq/L, Chloride 96 mEq/L, Bicarbonate 7 mEq/L, Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL.
Anion Gap calculation: 132 - (96 + 7) = 29 mEq/L (severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis with blood glucose < 200 mg/dL in a patient taking an SGLT2 inhibitor (Empagliflozin) is diagnostic of Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis (euDKA); do not be falsely reassured by non-hyperglycemic blood glucose.

releasedFindings: Serum Beta-hydroxybutyrate is markedly elevated at 6.8 mmol/L (normal < 0.5 mmol/L).
Urinalysis: 4+ Ketones, 4+ Glucose (persistent glucosuria despite euglycemia due to SGLT2 blockade).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirmed euDKA; immediately withhold SGLT2 inhibitor; initiate continuous IV Regular Insulin infusion (0.05-0.1 units/kg/hr) combined with early IV Dextrose (D5W or D10W with half-normal saline) to allow continuous insulin administration without precipitating hypoglycemia.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis (euDKA) secondary to SGLT2 Inhibitor (Empagliflozin)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Severe metabolic ketoacidosis (pH 7.14, HCO3 7, anion gap 29, beta-hydroxybutyrate 6.8 mmol/L) with normal or mildly elevated blood glucose (172 mg/dL) caused by SGLT2 inhibitor-mediated glucosuria and glucagon elevation.

clinicalScores.expectedResult: Severe High Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis (> 12 mEq/L)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Requires exact serum sodium, chloride, and bicarbonate.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Directly quantify circulating ketone body concentration.
Determine systemic pH, bicarbonate, and respiratory compensation.

immediateInterventions: Immediately discontinue Empagliflozin and Metformin
Initiate continuous IV Regular Insulin infusion (0.05-0.10 units/kg/hr)
Concurrently administer IV Dextrose (D5W or D10W in 0.45% NaCl) to prevent hypoglycemia while shutting off ketogenesis
Fluid resuscitation with balanced crystalloids
Frequent hourly blood glucose and 2-hour electrolyte/anion gap monitoring
definitiveTherapy: Continue insulin and dextrose infusion until anion gap normalizes (<= 12 mEq/L) and beta-hydroxybutyrate is < 0.6 mmol/L

strictContraindications: Withholding insulin because blood glucose is < 200 mg/dL (insulin is required to stop lipolysis and ketogenesis)
Re-starting SGLT2 inhibitor during acute illness
highRiskInteractions: Failing to give glucose while infusing insulin in euDKA induces profound hypoglycemia; failing to give insulin allows fatal acidosis progression.

criticalFailures.description: Dismissing DKA because blood glucose is below 200 mg/dL or withholding insulin therapy

guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: AACE Consensus Statement on the Association of SGLT2 Inhibitors and Diabetic Ketoacidosis

clinicalCategory: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia & Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Spontaneous bleeding from gums, severe epistaxis, and multiple large spontaneous ecchymoses
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Progressive bruising over 4 days; severe epistaxis started 3 hours ago

releasedFindings: CBC: WBC 3,200/uL, Hemoglobin 8.1 g/dL, Platelets 18,000/uL (profound thrombocytopenia).
Coagulation Profile: PT/INR 2.4, aPTT 48 seconds, Fibrinogen 65 mg/dL (severe hypofibrinogenemia, normal 200-400), D-Dimer > 20,000 ng/mL.
Physical exam: Active oozing from venipuncture sites and oral mucosa, diffuse confluent petechiae on extremities.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Fulminant Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) with severe hyperfibrinolysis and bleeding diathesis in a young patient with pancytopenia; high suspicion of Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL / AML M3).

progressiveStages.stageName: Peripheral Blood Smear & Pre-Genetic Treatment Priority
releasedFindings: Peripheral blood smear: 45% hypergranular promyelocytes with folded kidney-shaped nuclei and multiple Auer rods in bundles (classic 'faggot cells').
Bone marrow aspirate and cytogenetics / PML-RARA FISH are ordered and will take 24-48 hours.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Do NOT delay differentiation therapy for genetic or bone marrow confirmation. Immediate administration of All-Trans Retinoic Acid (ATRA / Tretinoin 45 mg/m2/day) within hours of clinical suspicion is mandatory to reverse life-threatening coagulopathy and prevent fatal intracranial hemorrhage.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL) with Severe Consumptive Coagulopathy (DIC)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Pancytopenia, severe consumptive coagulopathy (fibrinogen 65 mg/dL, elevated INR, D-dimer > 20,000), and peripheral smear demonstrating promyelocytes packed with Auer rod bundles ('faggot cells').

rankedDifferential.condition: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (Non-APL) with Sepsis-Induced DIC

clinicalScores.formula: Platelets (< 50k: +2) + Elevated D-Dimer (strong: +3) + Prolonged PT (> 6s: +2) + Fibrinogen (< 100 mg/dL: +1)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Calculated using all 4 standard ISTH coagulation parameters.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Identify Auer rod bundles ('faggot cells') and promyelocyte morphology.

immediateInterventions: Immediate administration of All-Trans Retinoic Acid (ATRA) 45 mg/m2/day PO without waiting for genetic confirmation
Aggressive blood product support: Cryoprecipitate transfusions targeting Fibrinogen >= 150 mg/dL
Platelet transfusions targeting Platelets >= 50,000/uL
Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) to correct INR < 1.5
Initiate Arsenic Trioxide (ATO) or anthracycline chemotherapy once ATRA is started
definitiveTherapy: Dual ATRA + Arsenic Trioxide (ATO) curative induction protocol

strictContraindications: Delaying ATRA therapy to await FISH or bone marrow aspirate results (delay causes fatal intracranial or pulmonary hemorrhage)
Withholding platelet or cryoprecipitate transfusions in active consumptive coagulopathy
highRiskInteractions: APL carries an early mortality rate of 20-30% primarily from catastrophic hemorrhagic stroke during the first 48 hours without ATRA.

criticalFailures.description: Delaying ATRA administration while awaiting confirmatory cytogenetics or bone marrow biopsy in suspected APL

mandatoryActions: Immediate ATRA administration prior to FISH confirmation

guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (APL Subtype)

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Severe right upper quadrant (RUQ) abdominal pain, scotoma (visual flashes), and throbbing headache
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Headache and epigastric discomfort started yesterday; worsened acutely this morning

releasedFindings: Repeat blood pressure 15 minutes later confirms severe range: 174/110 mmHg.
Physical exam: Marked 3+ patellar hyperreflexia with 3 beats of bilateral ankle clonus; pronounced RUQ subcostal hepatic tenderness.
Continuous fetal monitoring demonstrates reassuring fetal heart rate baseline of 140 bpm with moderate variability.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Preeclampsia with severe features; immediate hyperreflexia and clonus signal impending eclamptic convulsion; urgent administration of IV Magnesium Sulfate for seizure prophylaxis and emergent parenteral antihypertensive (IV Labetalol or Hydralazine) to prevent maternal intracranial hemorrhage.

releasedFindings: CBC: Platelets 62,000/uL (severe thrombocytopenia, baseline 210,000).
Liver Function Tests: AST 340 U/L, ALT 290 U/L (marked transaminitis, > 2x upper limit).
Hemolysis Markers: Total Bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL, LDH 820 U/L (elevated > 600 U/L), peripheral smear reveals schistocytes (microangiopathic hemolytic anemia).
Urinalysis: 3+ Protein (protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirmed HELLP Syndrome (Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets); definitive treatment is delivery; at 34 weeks gestation, expedite delivery following maternal stabilization; avoid maternal NSAIDs for pain.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Preeclampsia with Severe Features and HELLP Syndrome
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Severe gestational hypertension (178/112 mmHg) accompanied by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (schistocytes, LDH 820), transaminitis (AST 340), thrombocytopenia (platelets 62k), and clonus.

clinicalScores.scoreName: Mississippi Triple Class System for HELLP
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Requires exact platelet count and transaminases.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Complete Blood Count and Peripheral Smear
Comprehensive Hepatic Panel, LDH, and Coagulation Panel
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Confirm HELLP triad and rule out coagulopathy.
Assess fetal well-being and placental insufficiency.

immediateInterventions: IV Magnesium Sulfate: 4-6 gram loading dose over 20 minutes, followed by 1-2 g/hour continuous infusion for seizure prophylaxis
Immediate blood pressure control within 30-60 minutes: IV Labetalol (20 mg initial, doubling every 10 min) or IV Hydralazine (5-10 mg)
Target maternal blood pressure 140-150 / 90-100 mmHg (avoid precipitous drop which impairs uteroplacental perfusion)
Administer IM Betamethasone (12 mg) for fetal lung maturity if delivery can be delayed 24 hours safely
definitiveTherapy: Expedited delivery (induction vs cesarean section) once maternal blood pressure and seizure prophylaxis are stabilized

strictContraindications: Withholding magnesium sulfate in severe preeclampsia with clonus
Dropping systolic blood pressure precipitously below 130 mmHg (causes acute fetal distress from placental hypoperfusion)
Administering NSAIDs for postpartum analgesia in HELLP with thrombocytopenia
highRiskInteractions: Magnesium toxicity causes loss of deep tendon reflexes, respiratory depression, and cardiac arrest; monitor patellar reflexes hourly and keep calcium gluconate at bedside.

criticalFailures.description: Failing to initiate Magnesium Sulfate for seizure prophylaxis or failing to treat severe-range BP in preeclampsia

guidelineReferences.organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Deliberate overdose of approximately 30 tablets of Amlodipine 10mg (300 mg total) 2 hours ago
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Ingested 2 hours prior; brought by family with empty pill bottle

releasedFindings: Patient has received 3 liters of IV normal saline with NO improvement in blood pressure (BP remains 74/40 mmHg, MAP 51 mmHg).
Bedside glucose is 298 mg/dL (hyperglycemia is a classic marker of L-type calcium channel blockade of pancreatic islet beta-cells, correlating with overdose severity).
ECG: Junctional bradycardia at 48 bpm with PR prolongation and loss of P waves.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Severe calcium channel blocker overdose refractory to fluid loading; calcium channel antagonism impairs myocardial contractility, vascular smooth muscle tone, and pancreatic insulin secretion; fluid boluses must cease; initiate High-Dose Insulin Euglycemia Therapy (HIET) and IV Calcium immediately.

releasedFindings: Peripheral Norepinephrine at 20 mcg/min fails to restore MAP > 65 mmHg.
Patient becomes increasingly somnolent.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Activate toxicologic shock protocol: Administer IV Calcium Chloride (1-2 g via central line) or Calcium Gluconate (3-6 g); initiate High-Dose Insulin Therapy: regular insulin bolus 1 unit/kg IV followed by continuous infusion of 1 unit/kg/hr (titrated up to 5-10 units/kg/hr) with continuous D10W/D50W dextrose infusion to maintain euglycemia (glucose 150-250 mg/dL) and supplemental potassium to maintain K 2.8-3.2 mEq/L.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Severe Calcium Channel Blocker (Amlodipine) Toxicity with Refractory Vasoplegic Shock
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Massive Amlodipine ingestion (300 mg) causing junctional bradycardia, profound vasodilation refractory to 3L fluids, and characteristic stress hyperglycemia (298 mg/dL) due to pancreatic beta-cell calcium blockade.

clinicalScores.formula: Blood glucose > 200 mg/dL in non-diabetic CCB ingestion
clinicalScores.expectedResult: Severe Toxicity with High Risk of In-Hospital Mortality

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Monitor conduction blocks, bradycardia, and QT interval.
Prevent life-threatening hypoglycemia during high-dose insulin therapy.
Prevent fatal hypokalemia during high-dose insulin shift.

immediateInterventions: IV Calcium Chloride (1-2 g via central line) or Calcium Gluconate (3-6 g peripheral) repeated every 10-20 minutes
High-Dose Insulin Euglycemia Therapy (HIET): Regular insulin 1 unit/kg IV bolus + 1 unit/kg/hr infusion
Co-infusion of D10W or D50W to maintain target blood glucose 150-250 mg/dL
Norepinephrine or Epinephrine infusion for peripheral vascular resistance
Vasopressin (0.04 units/min) as adjunctive non-adrenergic vasopressor
definitiveTherapy: Venoarterial (VA) ECMO evaluation for refractory cardiogenic shock if HIET and vasopressors fail

strictContraindications: Continuing large volume fluid resuscitation (> 30 mL/kg) which causes acute pulmonary edema in cardiogenic/vasoplegic shock
Failing to administer concentrated dextrose during high-dose insulin therapy
Aggressive repletion of potassium when K > 3.0 mEq/L (insulin-driven shift does not reflect whole-body potassium depletion)
highRiskInteractions: HIET works as an inotrope by switching stressed myocytes to glucose metabolism; delayed initiation leads to refractory asystolic arrest.

criticalFailures.description: Failing to initiate high-dose insulin therapy or IV calcium in shock-refractory CCB overdose

guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: ACMT Position Statement: High-Dose Insulin Therapy for Calcium Channel Blocker Toxicity
